stem: A team wants to verify that a modal dialog works for keyboard-only users. Which test is most useful?

options.text: Tab through the open dialog and check focus stays inside and returns on close.
options.rationale: This checks the full keyboard interaction: entering the dialog, moving within it, and returning focus to the trigger.

options.text: Run an HTML validator and confirm that the dialog markup is well formed.
options.rationale: Valid markup can still leave a dialog unusable if focus escapes or never reaches the dialog.

options.text: Check the dialog's background and text colors with a contrast checker.
options.rationale: Contrast affects readability but does not show whether keyboard focus is managed correctly.

options.text: Confirm that the dialog element has an `aria-label` attribute in the source code.
options.rationale: A label helps announce the dialog but does not prove that keyboard users can enter, move within, or leave it.

explanation: Keyboard testing checks the full interaction: focus moves into the dialog, stays within it while it is open, and returns to the trigger when it closes. A validator, contrast check, or ARIA attribute check can pass while the dialog remains unusable by keyboard.

references.title: W3C WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices — Dialog (Modal) Pattern
